Source component: Global header (logo, college name, main nav, utility nav)
Supporting destinations: Site Toolbar; ACF: Site Layout (options page)
Why: Both establish CSU identity above local navigation. FYE uses a compact two-tier header, strong green strip and menu/search controls rather than the legacy horizontal mega-nav.
Transfer rules: Map main/local menus to FYE menu locations; configure network navigation inheritance, network home link and action button in Site Layout. Use toolbar for calendar, directory and news utility destinations.
Gaps: Audit mega-menu nesting, utility links, site-title destination and mobile behavior; toolbar is a selected set of utilities, not an arbitrary utility-menu replacement.

Why: The Secondary header preserves the clearest composition: title, introductory copy and action at left, featured image at right. The FYE brush texture replaces legacy circles.
Transfer rules: Set page_header_layout=secondary; transfer image to Featured Image, introductory body to page_header_description, actions to buttons[].link and headline to title/highlight_text_lines. Rebuild superhead as kicker where appropriate.
Gaps: Review long titles, caption toggle, cropping and contrast. Secondary-link hierarchy, subhead and legacy overlays are not a one-to-one field transfer.
Alternatives: Basic for text-only headers; Primary for image-led heroes.

Supporting destinations: Page Header: Secondary (side by side); Color Palette
Why: The same title/summary/CTA hierarchy fits FYE headers; Stalwart Slate is in FYE’s palette, but its supplied brush backgrounds are not identical to the legacy slate texture.
Transfer rules: Use Secondary when an image exists, Basic when absent. Select compatible title, text and background colors from Theme: Page Header.
Gaps: Do not assume every palette color has a matching brushstroke asset or header style. Check the actual selected header at full size.

Supporting destinations: Pattern: Call to Action Cover; Cover: Brushstroke variants
Why: Primary is the best theme-header match for RDC’s oversized image-led introduction. A Cover composition is the closer fallback when the media must remain behind the text.
Transfer rules: Image-only: use Primary plus description and buttons. Video: compose a core/cover video hero with heading, paragraph and button, then coordinate the theme header to avoid duplicate titles.
Gaps: The FYE header guide documents a featured image, not RDC’s video file/poster fields. Video, poster, playback and motion preferences require a custom composition and live validation.
Alternatives: Use Secondary if preserving the left text/right media split matters more than image dominance.

Why: Both are a short ancestor trail; FYE places it within page headers with different typography and separators.
Transfer rules: Map intended visibility to Page Options > breadcrumbs; confirm ancestor labels and URLs.
Gaps: Legacy show_breadcrumbs is per navigation settings; FYE’s documented toggle is a site-wide default. Per-page exceptions need verification.

Why: The notice banner has the same urgent communication purpose, with FYE adding a conspicuous Energy Green strip and dismissal control.
Transfer rules: Transfer headline/body into alert_content; configure alert_enabled, network push, scope, expiry and cookie duration.
Gaps: Legacy icon and severity are not documented destination fields. Test local/network precedence, expiry and dismissal; the destination guide’s GAP label conflicts with the source guide’s existing alert.

Supporting destinations: Page Header: Secondary (side by side); All Other WordPress Core Blocks
Why: FYE’s header navigation action box can preserve a selected set of section links, but it does not establish equivalence to the automatic left-hand page tree.
Transfer rules: Use user_action_box=nav with navigation_heading/navigation_menu and assign_nav_to_children for curated menus. Build a section-nav component if automatic hierarchy, current-page state and reset-to-page rules must remain.
Gaps: Sticky Nav only jumps to sections on the same page. core/page-list lists pages but is not a verified context-aware ancestor/sibling tree.
Alternatives: Use Sticky Nav Section only for long single-page content after intentional restructuring.

Supporting destinations: ACF: Site Layout (options page); ACF: Social Media (options page)
Why: Both combine grouped resource links, social destinations and institutional legal links. FYE emphasizes marketing text and a larger menu grid.
Transfer rules: Map footer links into footer_menu_left/center/right/extra; map social platforms and URLs to social_media_links; configure footer inheritance.
Gaps: Address, contact name/link and custom utility links have no equivalent fields listed in FYE. Preserve these in an approved contact area or extend the footer.

Why: A normal FYE page can preserve the content sequence. The legacy three-region layout (page tree, main content, sidebar) is a separate design requirement.
Transfer rules: Convert flex_slabs to blocks; compose main and contact/teaser column with core/columns if sidebar is required; build page-tree navigation separately.
Gaps: No matching ready-made Standard template is evidenced. Columns alone do not reproduce automatic navigation, sidebar widths or mobile reading order.
Alternatives: Prefer a simpler single-column page when contact and related content can move into the main flow.

Supporting destinations: Pattern: Media & Text; Pattern: Call to Action Cover; Call to Action: Cards | Traditional (Energy Green)
Why: Stacked full-width FYE groups, callouts and routing cards preserve the landing page’s sequence of promotional sections.
Transfer rules: Convert each flex_slabs row to the matching block/pattern; retain section order, anchors, actions and intended full/wide alignment.
Gaps: This is a composition recipe, not an identically named FYE template. Re-check permissions, content widths and spacing in the editor.

Supporting destinations: Columns: Divider variants; SOURCE Stories (default); Trumba Events
Why: The department introduction and full-width news/events area are reproducible, but the legacy nested content/sidebar layout has no demonstrated destination template.
Transfer rules: Compose introduction and main content, optional sidebar columns, then full-width CTA/facts/SOURCE/Trumba groups. Split flex_slabs and flex_slabs_wide into the correct sequence.
Gaps: Section navigation, sidebar rules and placement below the main region require an agreed reusable page pattern or custom template.

Why: Content Query has the closest search/filter/listing purpose and can present cards or tables. Its data contract differs from the external JavaScript people directory.
Transfer rules: If people become a registered post type, map groups to taxonomies, select postType, configure filters and create bio permalinks. Otherwise retain the external directory through a maintained integration.
Gaps: External directory data, person fields, search semantics and bio rendering are not supplied by Content Query. Verify table-column support for the required contact fields before selecting this route.

Preferred destination: Heading, Paragraph, List, Link, Quote and Table Defaults
Why: Core editorial blocks preserve paragraphs, lists, headings and inline links; font family and spacing change with the new theme.
Transfer rules: Convert HTML to semantic heading/paragraph/list/image blocks, wrapped in a constrained Group; retain a section heading before the body.
Gaps: Audit shortcodes, inline styles, embedded scripts and heading order individually. Do not flatten rich content into a single paragraph.

Why: Media & Text preserves a two-part promotional section with copy, action and image. The pattern supplies all three text/action elements.
Transfer rules: Move media to the right; map headline to heading, body to paragraph, button to Buttons and links to a separate list; set Group/Media & Text background.
Gaps: Brushstroke+ introduces an accent line and FYE typography; triangles/hexagons and exact legacy treatment do not transfer. Add caption outside the media slot if needed.

Source component: Callout slab — Standard, image left, gray
Why: Media-left with copy at right is the same information layout. A restrained background and Brushstroke style are closer than an image-overlay cover.
Transfer rules: Keep media on the left; use a Gray or neutral Group where allowed; transfer headline, body, actions and caption.
Gaps: Review gray/text contrast and mobile stacking; choose brush treatment deliberately rather than copying legacy background classes.

Why: The full-width Cover keeps the headline and action on a background image, matching the billboard purpose better than side-by-side Media & Text.
Transfer rules: Use image as Cover media; add heading, supporting paragraph, Buttons and any secondary links; set overlay opacity and focal point.
Gaps: The supplied starter does not include every legacy CTA field. Reverb is a collage treatment and is less visually similar to a single photographic billboard.
Alternatives: Ram Reverb Cover for an intentional campaign redesign, not the default conversion.

Supporting destinations: Columns: Divider variants; Pattern: Media & Text
Why: The repaired filmstrip shows an introduction above a row of three images. A Gallery inside a Group preserves this repeated-media structure; Columns can recreate the split headline and description.
Transfer rules: Compose a headline/action and description row, followed by a three-column Gallery. Preserve image count, crop ratio and mobile stacking. Use Media & Text only for an intentionally simplified single-image variant.
Gaps: No dedicated filmstrip style is listed. The Gallery example alone lacks the introduction/action area; create the complete reusable composition before conversion.

Why: A large image with a separate headline/action strip is closer to this variant than a slideshow.
Transfer rules: Build a full/wide Group containing Image and a heading/body/action group; Banner Strip can start a short headline/button band.
Gaps: The banner pattern alone has no large image or rich body. Review the exact strip placement and caption against the original; use Cover only if the source overlays text.

Source component: Routing Slab with Callouts — image teasers
Preferred destination: Call to Action: Cards | Traditional (Energy Green)
Supporting destinations: Call to Action: Cards | Traditional (Oval Green); ACF: Block: Call to Action
Why: Traditional CTA cards retain the image/headline/description/link structure and visible grid of routing choices. Oval Green feels closer to the darker legacy palette; Energy Green adopts the new emphasis.
Transfer rules: Map each callout to ctas[].image_icon/heading/description/link; superhead to kicker; preserve columns (1–4). Add the slab’s intro and section button outside the block.
Gaps: Per-item alignment and featured-card proportions may need adjustment. Swipe/Expanders change content visibility and interaction.
Alternatives: Choose Swipe only for intentional horizontal browsing; Expanders only when progressive disclosure is desired.

Source component: Routing Slab with Callouts — icon teasers, gray, centered
Supporting destinations: Pattern: Icon List; Call to Action: Icon List
Why: The unstyled CTA block is the better starting point for equal icon-led columns. Icon List is a good purpose match when a vertical action list is acceptable.
Transfer rules: Use CTA with icon images, item heading, description and link; preserve columns and wrap the section intro/background in a Group.
Gaps: The FYE default uses circular media; Icon List uses compact rows and its sample hides longer descriptions. Inspect actual content before switching from a grid.
Alternatives: Icon List pattern for concise actions; core/columns with image + heading + paragraph for exact centered grid control.

Why: Repeated Details preserve short question titles with expandable rich answers. Outline is closest to a restrained FAQ list; filled style is a stronger redesign.
Transfer rules: Map accordion headline to Details summary and body to nested blocks; retain section heading before the group.
Gaps: Do not assume mutually exclusive opening, legacy expand-all controls or anchor behavior. Check keyboard use and whether answers should start open.

Supporting destinations: Pattern: Icon List; Call to Action (default / no style)
Why: A core List keeps plain links most faithfully. CTA items suit links with a heading and supporting description; Icon List suits concise icon actions.
Transfer rules: Map link label/URL/target into List items; retain descriptions in adjacent text or CTA description; place the slab-wide icon with its heading.
Gaps: A single section icon is different from one icon per CTA. Avoid losing link descriptions in the compact Icon List style.

Why: Highlight List with Text already combines introductory copy/action with prominent numbers and captions. It is a stronger starting point than declaring a complete gap.
Transfer rules: Map fact headline to large number, super/subhead to contextual labels and caption; keep the introduction/button. For a horizontal stat row, rearrange number groups into Columns.
Gaps: No dedicated Fast Facts block or matching icon-box styles are listed. The supplied pattern stacks facts vertically; preserve icons using Image blocks and rebuild Icon A/B treatment if needed.

Supporting destinations: SOURCE Stories (default); ACF: Block: SOURCE Stories
Why: SOURCE Stories preserves the external CSU news-feed purpose and card content. Enterprise’s darker cards are closer to the legacy presentation than the bright default.
Transfer rules: Choose the CHHS SOURCE channel, translate categories/tags, story count, heading, SOURCE link/button and image ratio; use grid or feature layout according to the source.
Gaps: Guide labels disagree on direct/partial. Arbitrary legacy custom queries and tag/category operators are not proven equivalent; validate real returned stories. Content Query requires local posts and is not the default replacement.

Supporting destinations: List (Green Border + Multi-column); Pattern: Icon List
Why: Columns of titled link lists preserve the grouping of resource destinations more accurately than a single flat CTA collection.
Transfer rules: For each nested Link List create a Column/Group with heading, optional icon and links/descriptions; keep the parent section heading.
Gaps: No dedicated nested-list collection block is listed; maintain group labels, responsive reading order and any shared/reusable list relationships.

Why: Core Table preserves tabular relationships and caption, with FYE typography and borders replacing the legacy header styling.
Transfer rules: Convert row/cell data, header/footer sections and caption; use a separate section Heading. Create a synced pattern for genuinely shared tables.
Gaps: First-column row headers and reusable ACF table references need special handling; verify scope/header semantics and horizontal overflow, rather than assuming every ACF option transfers.

Supporting destinations: Slider (default / no style); ACF: Block: Slider
Why: Gallery is the closer visual and purpose match for a browsable collection visible at once. Slider is appropriate only when sequential browsing is intended.
Transfer rules: Map images, alt text, order and captions into core/gallery; carry intro/actions as separate blocks. If choosing Slider, map each image to slides[] and set type=images.
Gaps: Masonry layout and lightbox behavior are not established by the destination demo. Do not claim Slider preserves masonry or lightbox; validate enlargement behavior in WordPress.

Why: Trumba Events retains calendar-driven event titles/dates and calendar link, but FYE’s demo is a card grid rather than the embedded legacy spud placeholder.
Transfer rules: Map calendar identity to trumba_calendar_url, count to number_of_events and section heading/calendar button to their ACF fields.
Gaps: Destination uses a JSON feed rather than the legacy spud. Calendar filters, photo/list selection and custom views need feed-level validation; the static sample proves neither live data nor parity.

Why: A full-aligned Image preserves the purpose of a single wide photograph without introducing overlay text.
Transfer rules: Map image, alt text, caption and intended alignfull width; retain intrinsic ratio unless a deliberate crop is approved.
Gaps: Confirm theme content-container constraints and image quality.
Alternatives: Use Cover only if text overlay or background cropping is part of the actual source instance.

Why: Quote preserves quotation and attribution; its Energy Green rule changes the RDC treatment. Columns can preserve the optional accompanying portrait/image.
Transfer rules: Map body to Quote and source to citation; add image in an adjacent column and a Group background where needed.
Gaps: A single Quote block does not contain RDC’s optional image or color-scheme layout. Rich attribution links require careful conversion.

Why: A colored Group with structured contact text preserves the contact card’s purpose and dense labeled information.
Transfer rules: Heading + name/title/location/hours paragraphs; phone/email as usable links; preserve multiple contacts with groups/columns and social links.
Gaps: No dedicated Contact Info ACF block is documented. Reusable/sidebar placement needs a synced pattern and agreed page composition.

Preferred destination: Call to Action: Cards | Traditional (Oval Green)
Why: One-column CTA cards preserve image, heading, summary and destination. Image List offers a more compact alternative when summaries are short.
Transfer rules: Set CTA columns=1; map each teaser image/heading/summary/link; retain sidebar heading separately.
Gaps: Block availability does not create a sidebar region. Confirm card sizing inside the chosen column and move content into the page flow on mobile.

Supporting destinations: Pattern: Callout Heading; Pattern: Heading Highlight
Why: Heading plus kicker/subhead paragraphs preserves the three-level information hierarchy. Callout Heading offers a stylized superhead + display-title alternative.
Transfer rules: Use semantic heading for headline; separate small paragraph for superhead and paragraph for subhead; add icon or Separator only where needed.
Gaps: core/heading alone omits superhead, subhead and stroke/icon. The Callout Heading starter’s oversized italic type suits special features rather than every section.

Why: FYE Buttons support primary/outline actions and brand colors, retaining the action hierarchy with a different rounded/arrow treatment.
Transfer rules: Transfer label, URL, target and relationship; choose filled/outline styles and keep plain/fancy text links as inline links.
Gaps: Exact legacy arrow, sizes and fancy-link appearance are not guaranteed by core/button.

Preferred destination: Call to Action: Cards | Traditional (Energy Green)
Supporting destinations: ACF: Block: Call to Action; Content Query (default)
Why: CTA cards keep manually authored teaser image/title/summary/link content; Content Query is for teasers derived from local posts.
Transfer rules: Manual items → CTA repeater with 1–4 columns. Dynamic local-post items → Content Query with a defined post type and filter.
Gaps: Legacy featured/unequal cards need deliberate layout work; do not turn manual destinations into queries unless matching content exists.

Why: Image with figcaption retains the basic figure, caption and image purpose. The caption ACF switch applies separately to header featured images.
Transfer rules: Map media to Image, preserve alt text/caption/citation and choose aspect ratio; use image_caption for featured-image display where relevant.
Gaps: Retain credit/citation links explicitly; header caption toggle is not a global replacement for all figure captions.

Why: Details is a good match only for accordion disclosure. Tabs and modal dialogs have different interaction contracts and need separate decisions.
Transfer rules: Accordion → Details. Inspect Sticky Nav Item’s documented layout options before adopting tab-like layouts; retain/custom-build a tabs or dialog component when those interactions are required.
Gaps: The destination visual guide demonstrates neither full legacy tab behavior nor a modal equivalent. Focus management, keyboard navigation and dialog dismissal require live verification.

Supporting destinations: Embed (placeholder); All Other WordPress Core Blocks
Why: Upcoming-event teasers fit Trumba Events. Full calendar views and submission widgets have additional controls and workflows.
Transfer rules: Use Trumba Events only for list/teaser feeds. Inventory the ten named calendar/submission scripts and retain their calendar identities through a maintained embed/integration.
Gaps: Custom HTML is a container, not a script loader or full calendar replacement. Event submission, multiple calendar filters and custom spuds require separate testing.

Why: The filterable Content Query resembles directory browsing, but the four script files provide external data and bio pages.
Transfer rules: Choose external-directory integration or local people post type/taxonomy migration; map person detail fields and bio routes.
Gaps: Theme-switching can remove the shortcode’s script paths. Verify data refresh, filters, contact links and direct bio URLs before migration.

Why: Equipment booking and submission are application workflows, not content cards or an event-feed listing.
Transfer rules: Inventory all 42 equipment/calendar scripts; preserve equipment IDs, booking/submission destinations and required script initialization in a maintained plugin/block. Use a supported embed only if the service permits it.
Gaps: No FYE/Stalwart booking or equipment-form block is evidenced. Avoid mapping these to Trumba Events or CTA cards. Test actual submissions and confirmations in a test environment.

Supporting destinations: Embed (placeholder); All Other WordPress Core Blocks
Why: This group mixes news, announcements, course/catalog data, software checkout and lab widgets; it cannot have one reliable replacement.
Transfer rules: news-feed.js → SOURCE Stories. Review each remaining script independently: content-only material may become core blocks; service widgets need a supported embed or integration.
Gaps: Fourteen listed entries include .gitkeep, which is not a component. The guide does not demonstrate runtime behavior or all data contracts; classify each executable file before conversion.

Why: Inline media and blockquote shortcodes have clear core-block equivalents. Gravity Forms and local_script depend on retained plugins/integrations.
Transfer rules: inline_media → Image; custom_blockquote → Quote; gravityform → Gravity Forms block if installed, otherwise core/shortcode with the plugin active; local_script → maintained loader/integration.
Gaps: core/html does not implement arbitrary legacy shortcodes. Preserve form IDs, entry routing, notifications and script dependencies; counts in the guide cover post_content only.

Supporting destinations: ACF: Site Layout (options page); ACF: Page Options (options page); ACF: Social Media (options page)
Why: ACF is the data layer, not a visual component. Legacy flexible slabs become blocks/patterns while header and site options map into a smaller set of destination groups.
Transfer rules: Use the separate ACF crosswalk for individual groups and field transfer rules; preserve shared content as synced patterns where appropriate.
Gaps: Do not copy legacy group keys or flex_slabs metadata into new fields. No complete automatic conversion or runtime compatibility is claimed.
